items.title: Phrase Gym
items.text:
Phrase Gym is a local Python application with a browser interface for studying useful English phrases and keeping private recordings. Import a prepared phrase package, listen to its reference audio, record optional takes and replay them after reloading the app.

Daily offers due recall and new phrases within daily limits. First study is ungraded; on later learning days the app offers spoken recall with an honest self-rating and a scheduled return. Extra extends today's limits for another pass without erasing completed practice. The entry shows today's completed practice, the phrases studied today, a factual practice streak and the next return date. The Library finds phrases by lesson or meaning, shows their details and saved recordings, practises one chosen phrase, and deletes a phrase after confirmation. The app does not claim to measure fluency.

The server works on macOS and Linux. The MVP media player and recording experience target macOS browsers. Linux browser audio qualification is planned after the MVP.

Start with installation, then import a phrase package. The service listens only on loopback and keeps learner data in its local application-data directory.

For your external AI agent, pass along the preparation instructions and API handoff. See also private access, backup and restore, and the HTTP API reference.

items.title: Back up and restore local learning data
items.text:
Stop Coach, finish any pending browser recording saves, and quit Phrase Gym before copying files. Use the complete data directory, including phrase-gym.sqlite3, any -wal and -shm files, references/, and recordings/. The default is the OS user data directory for phrase-gym; on macOS it is ~/Library/Application Support/phrase-gym. If you launched with --data-dir, use that exact directory instead. Keep backups private because they contain learner recordings.

With both processes stopped, run these commands after setting DATA_DIR to the correct path:

DATA_DIR="$HOME/Library/Application Support/phrase-gym"
BACKUP_DIR="$HOME/Phrase Gym backups/phrase-gym-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$BACKUP_DIR")"
cp -Rp "$DATA_DIR" "$BACKUP_DIR"

Check that the backup contains the database, references/ and recordings/. To restore, stop both processes again and keep the current directory as a fallback. Copy the entire dated backup back into place; do not overwrite a live database or copy only its main file.

mv "$DATA_DIR" "$DATA_DIR.before-restore-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
cp -Rp "$BACKUP_DIR" "$DATA_DIR"

Start the same compatible Phrase Gym version. In the Library, check lesson and phrase counts and open representative phrase details for due dates and saved recordings. Play a representative reference and each saved take you need to confirm. If a copy fails, keep the fallback and backup untouched and retry while the app is stopped.

items.title: Importing prepared English phrases
items.text: Phrase Gym accepts one UTF-8 JSON object. Import format phrase-gym.package version 2 is the current package contract; earlier versions are rejected. The application makes no model or course-provider call during import; source links are attribution only and are never fetched.

items.title: Schema
items.text:
Field Requirement format Exactly phrase-gym.package version Exactly 2; other versions fail clearly package_id Stable ID for this exact package content; letters, digits, ., _, - source_id Stable identity for the course/unit/source source_label Short learner-readable attribution source_link Optional absolute HTTP(S) attribution URL learning_language en card_language en help_language en lessons 1–20 lessons with at most 50 phrases in total; an ordinary batch has 5–10 phrases

All reference audio for one package, whether Coach prepares it or an agent supplies it, must fit one 9 MiB budget: about 3.5 minutes of speech at 22,050 Hz. Fifty long sentences can exceed it; the import then fails with an error asking you to split the package, so keep packages short.

Each lesson has a stable lesson_id, a learner-readable title and one or more phrases. One package may contain several lessons; every phrase belongs to exactly one of them.

Each phrase requires:

Field Requirement item_id Stable ID, unique within the package text The fixed complete English wording explanation Short English meaning/use help shown after the answer cues One or two distinct situations; each has situation and an optional partner_line recall_hints Two to six distinct hand-prepared hints of one or two words, at most 40 characters each, never the whole phrase usage_contexts One to six distinct short searchable uses, such as small talk or greetings accepted_variants Optional genuinely suitable alternatives for the same intention detailed_explanation Optional longer native-language help shown on request

Unknown fields are rejected, and validation names the lesson, phrase and field to correct.

source_id plus lesson_id is permanent lesson identity: a later package can add phrases to that lesson only with the same title. source_id plus item_id is permanent phrase identity. Repeating it while that phrase is in the Library is rejected without overwriting it. To replace a defective phrase, delete it in the Library or its details after confirmation, then import the corrected phrase in a new package; it becomes a new phrase with fresh reference audio.

The generated machine-readable request schema is available at frontend/openapi.json. A complete three-lesson file is examples/meeting-phrases.json.

items.title: Instruction for an external preparation agent
items.text:
Prepare 5–10 useful fixed English phrases from the supplied course material as one Phrase Gym package version 2. Preserve the course wording, group phrases into the course's lessons, and give the package, source, every lesson and every phrase a stable searchable ID. For each phrase provide the complete English text, a short plain-English meaning/use explanation, one or two distinct short situations that communicate the intention without revealing the target wording, two or more hand-picked recall hints of one or two words that help retrieve this exact wording (not simply its first or last word), and short usage_contexts a learner might search for. Add a preceding partner line only when natural. Include only genuinely acceptable variants. Use the "So far, so good." phrase in the example file as the model. Do not add raw words, variable slots, dialogue graphs, invented quotations, audio URLs, or fields outside the documented schema. Return JSON only, then inspect every phrase for intended meaning, natural cues, answer leakage, useful hints and contexts, and suitable alternatives before giving it to the learner.

Phrase Gym validates structure, not teaching quality. The learner or a semantic reviewer still checks real prepared content separately.

items.title: Piper voice
items.text:
The separately running Coach expects PHRASE_GYM_PIPER_CONFIG to name a private JSON file outside the repository. Piper itself is a separately pinned environment.

On the learner's macOS machine, create that private environment outside every repository with the same Python minor version as Phrase Gym and these exact packages:

PIPER="$HOME/Library/Application Support/io.github.andgineer.Phrase-Gym/piper-1.8.0"
python3.13 -m venv "$PIPER"
"$PIPER/bin/python" -I -m pip install --no-deps --only-binary=:all: \
  piper-tts==1.8.0 onnxruntime==1.31.0 flatbuffers==25.12.19 numpy==2.5.4 \
  packaging==25.0 pathvalidate==3.3.1 protobuf==7.36.2
"$PIPER/bin/python" -I -m pip check

Download the selected model and adjacent JSON configuration outside the repository, calculate both SHA-256 values, and create the private voice file with this shape:

{
  "executable": "/absolute/path/to/piper/bin/python",
  "runtime_version": "1.8.0",
  "model": "/absolute/path/to/en_US-ljspeech-medium.onnx",
  "model_sha256": "64-lowercase-hex-digits",
  "config": "/absolute/path/to/en_US-ljspeech-medium.onnx.json",
  "config_sha256": "64-lowercase-hex-digits",
  "voice": "en_US-ljspeech-medium",
  "locale": "en-US"
}

Coach verifies the exact installed piper-tts version against runtime_version, model/config hashes, and English locale. It streams the selected interpreter's output under hard 8 MiB audio, 64 KiB diagnostic, and 60-second limits, terminates a process that exceeds a bound, and sends WAV references to the Phrase Gym API for atomic publication. Automated tests use a silent fake child and never invoke real Piper.

items.title: API handoff
items.text:
POST /api/imports accepts { "package": <version-2 package> }. The server validates and stores a text-only request before returning pending. Start phrase-gym coach separately to prepare it. GET /api/imports and GET /api/imports/{package_id} report pending, preparing, added, or error. Retry an error or interrupted preparation with POST /api/imports/{package_id}/retry; retrying the same package content returns its existing status. Coach retrieves work and returns a complete result through the API; it never opens the application database.

An external agent that already has audio can call POST /api/imports with package and references, a map from each item_id to base64-encoded mono 16-bit PCM WAV bytes. Every phrase must have one complete playable reference, at most 8 MiB, and all references together must fit a 9 MiB audio budget. Base64 expands the audio by about one third; the 9 MiB budget leaves room for phrase data within the API's 16 MiB request limit. These are per-package request limits, not a limit on your library: split larger courses across packages, reusing lesson identities and titles. This publishes the batch atomically and returns added without Coach. A malformed or missing reference identifies the item and rejects the whole request. Retrying identical package and audio returns the original result; changed content under the same package_id is rejected. The browser paste/file import accepts text-only packages and shows pending Coach work while it is offline.

items.title: Installation and launch
items.text:
Use Python 3.13 and uv. Published packages include the built browser client:

uv tool install phrase-gym --upgrade --python 3.13

Until a release is published, install from a source checkout:

uv sync --frozen
npm --prefix frontend ci
npm --prefix frontend run build

Start the server; Piper is not required to launch it:

phrase-gym run

For a source checkout, use uv run phrase-gym run instead. Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Use phrase-gym run --help for the port and data-directory options. Keep voice files and learner recordings outside the source checkout. Actual microphone and headset acceptance requires attended testing on the learner's MacBook.

For text-only imports, configure a local English Piper voice and run Coach in another terminal:

PHRASE_GYM_PIPER_CONFIG=/absolute/path/to/piper-voice.json phrase-gym coach

For a source checkout, use uv run phrase-gym coach. Coach receives pending imports through Phrase Gym's API and generates reference audio. Imports with complete reference audio do not need Coach. Piper uses the separately pinned private environment described in the import guide.

The install-coach, uninstall-coach, and deploy commands report that they are unavailable. The optional coach and deploy extras are reserved for future preparation and provisioning features. The core server and help need only the lean installation.

For access from another device, see private Tailscale access. Keep a private backup of your learning data.

items.title: Private Tailscale access
items.text:
With Tailscale already connected, from a source checkout run uv run inv run --build --tailscale. The task points the existing HTTPS Serve route at 127.0.0.1:8000 and passes the exact machine origin to Phrase Gym. The backend remains on loopback; only devices permitted by your Tailscale policy can use this shared library. This does not enable public Funnel access. Run Coach with PHRASE_GYM_PIPER_CONFIG when preparing text-only material. The server starts without Piper and continues to serve study and replay while Coach is stopped.

Use tailscale serve status to inspect the route. Stop an old Phrase Gym process before starting the replacement; retain its data directory and recordings. On iPhone, use the HTTPS machine URL with Tailscale connected. Microphone permission and actual playback still need attended checks.

items.title: HTTP API reference
items.text:
A running Phrase Gym server exposes its generated HTTP contract at /openapi.json and interactive API documentation at /docs. Adjust the host and port if your server uses another address. External agents can read that contract to validate requests against the running version.

For preparation instructions, the package schema and submission/status endpoints, see Importing prepared English phrases.
